title: India complete historic double at Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship
description: India defeated Sri Lanka 54-20 to win the inaugural men’s Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship 2026 in Ahmedabad. Aditya Shinde led the attack with 10 raid points, while Yogesh Dahiya impressed in defence. India completed a historic double after the women’s team also won gold earlier. The men finished unbeaten, securing eight victories throughout the tournament.

title: Thousands rally in Manipur against recent killings, ethnic conflict
Strangled after drinks, body dumped in lake: Wife, 2 lovers kill husband in Telangana
description: A woman named Gummadi Savitha conspired with her lovers to murder her husband, Gummadi Kashiram. They lured him out under the pretense of drinking liquor on October 23, 2026. Once he was intoxicated, one lover strangled him while the other restrained him. Afterward, they disposed of his body in a lake to conceal the crime. The police have arrested all three individuals and have charged them accordingly.

title: Tear gas, water cannon, clashes: France hit by third weekend of protests
description: Nationwide protests in France attracted an estimated 320,000 participants voicing concerns over rising living costs and government policies. Fresh clashes erupted between police and protesters in Paris, leading to the use of tear gas. While many protests were peaceful, some demonstrators engaged in violent confrontations with security forces. Participants included a coalition of youth organisations seeking change regarding economic inequality and public services.

title: 'Will deal with Modi, Shah': Rahul explains why CEC Gyanesh Kumar is his first target
description: Explaining why the INDIA bloc has upped its attack on the election chief, Rahul Gandhi accused him of acting as an instrument of the ruling establishment and warned that those allegedly involved in undermining democratic institutions would be held accountable. The leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha warned the CEC and other officials against assuming that constitutional immunity would shield them from accountability.

title: Oleshky evacuees reach Ukraine after taking a detour through Russia
description: The evacuation of Oleshky's residents marks a significant humanitarian effort as they navigated through Crimea, Russia, and Belarus during a temporary ceasefire. With the aid of buses, this complex journey, affirmed by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, reunited families after long separations. The perilous living conditions and food scarcity pushed these individuals to leave their homes, ultimately finding refuge in the Chernihiv region of Ukraine.

title: WTC Standings: Australia slip after series defeat; where are India?
description: Australia slipped to third place in the World Test Championship standings after losing their Test series 2-1 to South Africa. The defeat also cost them the No.1 spot in the ICC Test rankings, with South Africa taking over. New Zealand lead the WTC table, while India sit fourth. Australia next face New Zealand at home in December.

description: In Cooch Behar district, a woman named Priya Pal lost her baby after an assault on her husband. The alleged attack involved suspected BJP workers who targeted her husband, Debajit Barman, while he was returning home. After the incident, both Priya and Debajit were admitted to the hospital for treatment. Two suspects have been arrested, while a search is ongoing for additional accused individuals.

title: Binance replenishes 90% of stolen crypto, says it will absorb financial losses
description: In a commendable move, Binance has restored 90 percent of the cryptocurrency assets lost due to a recent security breach. The exchange has pledged to handle the financial repercussions internally, ensuring customers are unaffected. Withdrawals are set to resume on Sunday, November 1, as Binance reinforces its commitment to transparency regarding its reserves.

title: 'Secret meets on foreign soil': PM Modi says opposition conspiring to divide nation
description: Accusing opposition of ripping apart the dignity and boundaries of the Constitution, PM Modi said: "Social media is being weaponised to spread rumours and to malign India's image. The citizens of the country must handle this together. We have eliminated Naxalism in far-flung areas, but the threat of 'Dimagi Naxalism' has not yet been averted from the nation."

Sanjay Gupta's last rites held at Versova crematorium: Celebs arrive to pay last respects
description: The film industry is mourning the sudden loss of filmmaker Sanjay Gupta, who died after suffering a head injury at his residence in Mumbai. Tributes have flooded in from fellow artists and friends, underscoring his significant influence on their careers. At his funeral held at the Versova crematorium, close associates like Sanjay Dutt and Milap Zaveri reflected on Gupta's remarkable contributions, leaving the cinema world facing a profound loss.

title: Narang, Usha, Nehwal among 27 names in Draft List for IOA SOM Elections
description: The draft list of nominations has been released for the 2026 IOA Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (SOM) elections, scheduled for November 9. The list contains 27 candidates—15 men and 12 women—including prominent sporting names such as Gagan Narang, PT Usha, Saina Nehwal, Yogeshwar Dutt and Anju Bobby George.

title: 'Musalmaan hone ki saza': Azam Khan arrested by ED minutes after he gets out of jail
description: Azam Khan was arrested by the Enforcement Directorate just after being released from Rampur jail. He had spent nearly 11 months in custody due to legal issues. His son, Abdullah Azam, was released simultaneously but was not taken into custody. The arrest relates to a 2019 case involving allegations of financial wrongdoing and land-grabbing activities. Khan responded emotionally, asserting that his arrest is due to his identity as a Muslim.

Island nation’s treaty with Australia raises concerns over loss of cultural heritage
description: Tuvalu's recent treaty with Australia allows its citizens to migrate for work and study opportunities abroad. While migration offers new options, concerns exist regarding the preservation of cultural heritage. Traditional buildings and construction skills might be at risk as populations shift. Researchers are documenting Tuvalu's architectural history through photographs and digital models. Decisions on migration and land use should integrate considerations of cultural heritage and community identity.

title: Australia hammered by Harmer in Cape Town as South Africa take series 2-1
description: Chasing a target of 288, Australia were bowled out for 111 in the second session on the final day. The result also took South Africa above Australia to the top of the Test world rankings for the first time since January 2016.

title: Ireland's Indian-origin pacer Moondra creates cricket history with 6/26 figures
description: Ireland pacer Jai Moondra made history against Namibia in the fourth ODI, taking six wickets for just 26 runs in 10 overs. His performance set a new record for Ireland’s best bowling figures in international cricket, surpassing Josh Little’s 6/36. Ireland won the match by 130 runs to level the five-match series 2-2, with the decider scheduled for Sunday.

title: Patrick Mahomes and wife Brittany bring holiday joy to Kansas City families
description: In December 2023, Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes rallied together for EarlyStart's Clothing Kits for Kids campaign, aimed at aiding Kansas City families with much-needed winter apparel. Their charity, 15 and the Mahomies, generously provided several clothing kits to those in need. A thankful mother applauded the couple's dedication to supporting children and schools throughout the festive season, highlighting the event's role in fostering community solidarity.

title: Kim Jong Un's cyber army: How North Korea's hackers steal billions for regime
description: North Korea has developed a sophisticated cyberwar machine enabling it to target financial institutions worldwide. The country's state-sponsored hackers increasingly rely on social engineering and malware to infiltrate cryptocurrency companies. Cyber operations are essential for generating funds due to international sanctions and economic isolation. Reports suggest that North Korea has stolen billions in cryptocurrency through extensive cybercriminal activity. These actions directly support its military programs and other state priorities.

title: 'Won't forgive and forget': Rahul Gandhi at CEC's 'public impeachment' event
Jewish banker's heirs sue Sotheby's over £1.2m 'Nazi-looted' painting
description: A prized artwork by Camille Pissarro is embroiled in a contentious legal battle initiated by the heirs of Salomon Flavian. They assert that the piece was taken by the Nazis during WWII and argue that they were not adequately involved in a prior settlement. Sotheby’s counters, insisting the sale was aboveboard and legally sound. This dispute highlights ongoing hurdles in recovering Holocaust-era property and ensuring rightful family representation.

title: 'Keep Rahul mock PM for life': BJP's dig at INDIA bloc's 'public impeachment' of CEC
description: BJP national spokesperson Sambit Patra, who is MP from Puri Lok Sabha constituency, called the "mock parliament" a "drama", and highlighted that the Speical Intensive Revision (SIR) was ongoing and substantiated the claims around the "13 crore delted voters". Earlier, Amit Shah challenged the INDIA bloc to discuss the issue during a special session of Parliament.

title: 13-year-old Goan girl turns backyard moringa into powder business
description: During her summer break, Grace de Souza, a talented teenager from Goa, tapped into her entrepreneurial spirit by producing moringa powder from the leaves of her family's two moringa trees. Her efforts have proven fruitful, with earnings nearing Rs 3,000 from selling 20 packets. Inspired by this success, Grace plans to sustain her small business even when school resumes, embracing the lessons of hard work and responsibility.

title: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce donate $1 million to feed 2.4 million New Yorkers
description: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce donated $26 million to charities across the US, supporting food banks, children's hospitals, education and animal welfare. Their $1 million contribution to New York's City Harvest is expected to help provide food to more than 2.4 million residents this summer. Several nonprofit leaders expressed shock and gratitude after learning about the unexpected gifts, which arrived as many communities face growing financial and food insecurity.
